dataDescription: 94 method-condition rows: Recorded Replay and updated Residual PPO in 39 known regression conditions and 8 predeclared held-out conditions. Geometric-completion-window and full-episode metrics are separate columns. All values are measured simulation results; failed cases remain in the data, while paired posture plots include only jointly strict-successful conditions.

figures.title: Evaluation conditions
figures.alt: Scatter plot of initial gap targets and friction scales for 39 known regression conditions and 8 held-out conditions at a 100 mm step height.
figures.caption: 100 mm evaluation design. Each marker is one condition shared by the two compared methods. Gap is the configured initial target. The 39-condition set was already used for development and diagnosis; the eight predeclared held-out conditions were evaluated only after model selection was frozen. This is evaluation coverage, not the 32-episode training distribution.
figures.reading: Separate the known-condition results from the held-out results when discussing generalization.

figures.title: Completion under two outcome definitions
figures.alt: Grouped bars show common completion and strict success: Recording 31/39 and 27/39 versus PPO 37/39 and 32/39 on known cases; Recording 6/8 and 6/8 versus PPO 8/8 and 6/8 on held-out cases.
figures.caption: 100 mm complete-controller results. Strict success is the intersection of common completion and native success. Bars show condition counts divided by each cohort size, with exact counts above the bars. These suites do not provide independent repeated-run uncertainty estimates; no confidence intervals or statistical significance are asserted.
figures.reading: The known regression set improves under both definitions. On held-out conditions, the extra common completions do not produce a higher strict-success count.

figures.title: Paired body-inclination measurements
figures.alt: Two scatter plots compare total-tilt RMS for Recording on the horizontal axis and PPO on the vertical axis. All 25 known-case pairs and all 5 held-out pairs lie below the equality line.
figures.caption: Total-tilt RMS from native 120 Hz measurements, through each method's geometric completion. Only conditions in which both methods strictly succeed are shown: 25 of 39 known conditions and 5 of 8 held-out conditions. Each point is one matched condition. The percentages are means of per-case relative reductions, not reductions of the cohort means, and do not include failed cases.
figures.reading: All plotted pairs have lower tilt RMS with updated PPO. This conditional posture result is evaluated alongside completion, not in place of it.

figures.title: Posture tradeoffs on the held-out pairs
figures.alt: Individual paired percentage changes across five held-out cases show lower total tilt RMS and roll RMS but higher peak total tilt and pitch RMS for every pair.
figures.caption: The same five jointly strict-successful held-out pairs and geometric-completion windows as the paired scatter. Change = 100 × (PPO / Recording − 1). Dots are individual conditions; diamonds are means of per-case changes. Negative values indicate lower measured magnitude. Mean changes are −14.5% total-tilt RMS, +16.1% peak tilt, −20.2% roll RMS and +7.8% pitch RMS.
figures.reading: Lower total-tilt RMS mainly accompanies lower roll RMS in these pairs. Every peak and pitch RMS is higher; the result does not establish uniform improvement across posture metrics.

figures.title: Roll and pitch during nominal wheel transfers
figures.alt: Nominal 100 mm roll and pitch RMS by front-right, front-left, rear-right and rear-left wheel transfer. PPO lowers roll in all four groups; rear-right pitch rises from 4.77 to 5.69 degrees.
figures.caption: Original 100 mm nominal figure, grid_d1_mu1, using native 120 Hz RMS over identical fixed Recorded Replay windows for both methods. FR, FL, RR and RL denote front-right, front-left, rear-right and rear-left. FR pools two transfers by sample-weighted squared angles before taking the square root; it is not an average of two RMS values. These are evaluation event windows, not PPO training stages.
figures.reading: The largest roll change is in the rear-right group: 18.49° → 13.05°. Rear-right pitch moves in the other direction: 4.77° → 5.69°.
